reasoning_traces.think:
GTA operates in two stages: first, the Tracklet Splitter applies DBSCAN clustering on ReID embeddings to isolate identity-pure fragments from potentially mixed tracklets. This addresses mix-up errors by enforcing intra-tracklet homogeneity. Second, the Tracklet Connector builds a distance matrix using temporal overlap and mean pairwise cosine similarity of embeddings, then applies hierarchical clustering with spatial constraints to merge compatible fragments. The spatial constraint enforces physical plausibility by forbidding large inter-frame displacements, preventing teleportation artifacts. The method’s robustness stems from its modular design: it can be applied as a post-processing layer to any tracker, improving performance without altering the base model. Its dual nature—splitting and connecting—mirrors the duality of object identity and motion in multi-object tracking. Failure modes include misclassification under poor ReID quality or incorrect spatial thresholds in dynamic camera setups.
